_about: This is the SM-1 target library: starting targets with wording written for the practice, each one editable after it is placed on the student's sheet.

entries.def: Begins the assigned task (materials out and pencil, eyes, or hands on the work) within 1 minute of the direction to start, with no more than one reminder.
entries.ex: Writes their name on the worksheet within a minute of “Start your math page”
entries.nex: Rolls a pencil on the desk for 3 minutes after the direction

entries.def: Begins the first item of the assigned task (writing, reading, typing, or opening the named material) within 1 minute of the direction to start, without a second prompt.
entries.ex: Opens the laptop to the assignment and types the first answer within a minute of the bell work direction
entries.nex: Keeps talking to a peer until the teacher repeats the direction

entries.def: At each check during independent work (for example, a signal every 5 minutes), eyes are on the task materials and the student is writing, reading, using the materials, or asking about the task.
entries.ex: Is writing the next spelling word when the signal sounds
entries.nex: Is looking out the window with the pencil down when the signal sounds

entries.def: Completes all assigned items, or the amount agreed for the student, by the end of the work period and places the work in the finished tray or hands it to the adult.
entries.ex: Answers all 10 problems and puts the page in the tray before the timer ends
entries.nex: Answers 4 of 10 problems and puts the page in the desk

entries.def: During independent work, stays at the assigned desk with voice off or at a whisper heard only by the person next to them, except to ask the adult a question after raising a hand.
entries.ex: Works silently at the desk and raises a hand to ask a question
entries.nex: Sings or calls out across the room during independent work

entries.word: I follow directions the first time
entries.def: Starts doing what the adult asked within 10 seconds of the first direction and completes it, without a repeated direction.
entries.ex: Puts the book away and lines up within 10 seconds of “Books away, line up”
entries.nex: Says “in a minute” and starts only after the direction is given a third time

entries.def: While the teacher is talking to the group or to the student, eyes are toward the teacher or the named material, voice is off, and hands are still or on the named material for the whole talk.
entries.ex: Looks at the board and stays quiet while the teacher explains the activity
entries.nex: Talks to a neighbor while the teacher gives the directions

entries.def: When an adult tells the student about a change in the plan or schedule, the student answers in a calm voice (says “okay,” nods, or asks a question) and goes to the new activity within 1 minute.
entries.ex: Says “okay” when recess moves inside and walks to the gym with the class
entries.nex: Shouts and drops to the floor when told recess is inside today

entries.def: When a change to the day's schedule is announced, the student responds at a conversational voice level (acknowledges it or asks about the new plan) and begins the new activity within 2 minutes.
entries.ex: Asks “When is art now?” and then starts the substitute activity
entries.nex: Argues for 5 minutes and refuses to start the substitute activity

entries.word: I move to the next activity
entries.def: Within 1 minute of the transition signal, puts away the current materials and walks to the next activity or area, with no more than one reminder.
entries.ex: Puts crayons in the bin and walks to the carpet within a minute of the bell
entries.nex: Keeps coloring at the table after the class has moved to the carpet

entries.word: I stop when time is up
entries.def: When the timer sounds or the adult says time is up for a chosen activity, the student stops and puts away or hands over the item within 30 seconds, using a calm voice and body.
entries.ex: Turns off the tablet and hands it to the adult when the timer rings
entries.nex: Holds the tablet away from the adult and keeps playing after the timer

entries.def: When unable to continue a task, the student raises a hand, shows the help card, or says “Can you help me?” and waits at the task for the adult, instead of leaving the task or putting it away.
entries.ex: Raises a hand and says “I don't get number 3” when stuck
entries.nex: Crumples the worksheet and puts their head down when stuck

entries.def: Requests a break by handing over the break card or saying “Break, please” in a calm voice, goes to the agreed break area, and returns to the activity within 1 minute of the break timer ending.
entries.ex: Hands the break card to the teacher, sits in the break corner, returns when the timer ends
entries.nex: Leaves the room without asking or stays in the break area after the timer

entries.def: When one of the student's listed triggers occurs (for example, a hard task, a “no,” or a peer conflict), the student uses a taught strategy (slow breaths, counting to 10, squeezing a fidget, the calm corner) within 1 minute and returns to the activity.
entries.ex: Takes three slow breaths after losing a game and joins the next round
entries.nex: Throws the game pieces after losing and refuses the next round

entries.def: When told to wait or when another person has the turn or the adult's attention, the student stays in place with hands to self and voice quiet for the stated wait time, without grabbing, calling out, or repeating the request.
entries.ex: Stands in line with hands down until the teacher says “Your turn”
entries.nex: Grabs the ball from a peer or calls the teacher's name over and over

entries.def: When an adult says “no,” “not now,” or “wait,” the student responds within 10 seconds in a calm voice (says “okay,” nods, or picks another choice) and asks again no more than once.
entries.ex: Says “okay” and picks the puzzle when told the tablet is not available
entries.nex: Cries and asks for the tablet again and again after hearing “no”

entries.def: When a request is denied, the student responds at a conversational voice level within 10 seconds (acknowledges it, asks when it will be possible, or chooses another option) and does not argue or repeat the request more than once.
entries.ex: Says “Fine, can I go at lunch?” when told no to leaving early
entries.nex: Argues and raises their voice for several minutes after the answer

entries.def: When an adult points out a mistake, the student looks at the work, says “okay” or nods, and starts the correction within 30 seconds without tearing, erasing all of it, or leaving the task.
entries.ex: Erases the backwards 3 and writes it again after the teacher points to it
entries.nex: Tears up the paper when the teacher points to the mistake

entries.def: When an adult gives a correction on work or behavior, the student listens without interrupting, says “okay” or asks one question about it, and makes the change or carries on with the task within 1 minute.
entries.ex: Says “okay” and rewrites the thesis sentence after the teacher's comment
entries.nex: Says “That's not wrong” and stops working on the essay

entries.word: I keep safe hands and feet
entries.def: Hands, feet, and objects stay to self for the whole period: no hitting, kicking, pushing, grabbing, or throwing objects toward people, including when upset or waiting.
entries.ex: Keeps hands in lap while waiting next to a peer on the carpet
entries.nex: Pushes a peer in line; throws a pencil toward a classmate

entries.def: Remains seated or standing within the assigned place (desk, carpet spot, or taped area) for the whole period, except when given permission or using the break card.
entries.ex: Stays at the desk while the class works; stays on the carpet spot during meeting
entries.nex: Walks to the window without asking; crawls under the table

entries.def: Speaks to peers using polite or neutral words (please, thank you, names, helpful comments) for the whole period, with no name-calling, teasing, threats, or swearing.
entries.ex: Says “Can I have a turn, please?” to a peer
entries.nex: Calls a peer a name after losing a game

entries.def: During group lessons, raises a hand and waits to be called on before speaking, with no calling out during the lesson.
entries.ex: Raises a hand and answers after the teacher says their name
entries.nex: Shouts the answer before the teacher calls on anyone

entries.def: During class discussion or group work, waits until the speaker finishes or the student is called on before speaking, with no talking over a peer or the teacher.
entries.ex: Waits for a peer to finish the point, then adds their own
entries.nex: Talks over a peer who is answering the teacher

entries.def: Stays about an arm's length from others when sitting, standing in line, or talking, and touches others' bodies or belongings only after asking and getting a yes.
entries.ex: Stands an arm's length behind the peer in line
entries.nex: Leans on a peer during circle; takes a peer's pencil without asking

entries.def: Speaks to adults at a conversational voice level, using polite or neutral words, for the whole period, including when disagreeing, with no swearing, insults, or yelling.
entries.ex: Says “I don't agree, can we talk after class?” to the teacher
entries.nex: Swears at the teacher when asked to put the phone away
